answer: The evidence does not provide a stable conclusion for the broad hypothesis that search rates differ across known race categories. Although all 94 available estimates were statistically significant, the result depends strongly on the race contrast: the median standardized effect was -0.279 for all-pairwise/global comparisons but 0.196 for comparisons versus white, with a 74.7% inference-flip and sign-reversal rate.
rationale: There is evidence of race-related differences under the available specifications, but the major contrast-structure dependence makes the broad claim non-comparable across specifications. In addition, 66 of 160 universes were unavailable, so the evidence is incomplete rather than sufficient for a definitive overall assessment.
key_evidence: 94 estimates had confidence intervals and none were indeterminate; 57 were significantly negative and 37 significantly positive.
The median standardized effect was -0.2788 for all-pairwise comparisons and -0.2788 for the global omnibus comparison, versus 0.1956 when each category was compared with white.
Changing contrast structure produced a 0.7467 inference-flip rate and a 0.7467 sign-reversal rate.
Only 94 of 160 universes were available; 66 were unavailable.
refinement_reason: The hypothesis combines substantively different race-contrast structures and search-outcome definitions. Race contrast choice is highly consequential, and the outcome choice changes the median standardized effect from -0.2788 for any recorded search to approximately -0.046 to -0.048 for the other outcomes.
suggested_hypotheses: Among all recorded stops, known race categories differ in search_conducted rates when assessed using a prespecified all-pairwise or global omnibus comparison.
Among all recorded stops, each specified known race category differs from white in person-search rates, with category-specific effects reported separately.
Among all recorded stops, known race categories differ in vehicle-search rates under a prespecified race-contrast structure.
caveats: The supplied summaries do not identify which specific race categories drive the positive or negative results.
The large contrast-structure sensitivity limits direct comparability of the standardized effects.
Non-significance cannot be inferred for unavailable universes; 66 of 160 universes were unavailable.

analysis_universe.label: Analysis universe
analysis_universe.rationale: Which recorded stops should be included in the comparison?  [found by: direct]

all_recorded_rows.label: All recorded rows
all_recorded_rows.description: Include every row in the dataset, regardless of date or county_name, provided subject_race and the selected search outcome are usable.

period_all_counties.label: 2002–2015 stops in all counties
period_all_counties.description: Keep rows with date from 2002-01-01 through 2015-12-31 inclusive, regardless of county_name.

period_durham_county.label: 2002–2015 Durham County stops
period_durham_county.description: Keep rows with date from 2002-01-01 through 2015-12-31 inclusive and county_name equal to Durham County.

race_definition.label: Race-category definition and unknown handling
race_definition.rationale: Which column and category set should define the known race groups?  [found by: direct]

subject_race_known_only.label: Recorded subject_race, known categories only
subject_race_known_only.description: Use subject_race and retain only black, white, hispanic, asian/pacific islander, and other; exclude rows coded unknown or missing.

subject_race_with_unknown.label: Recorded subject_race including unknown
subject_race_with_unknown.description: Use subject_race with black, white, hispanic, asian/pacific islander, other, and unknown as separate comparison categories; exclude only missing values.

raw_race_ethnicity_recode.label: Reconstructed race from raw fields
raw_race_ethnicity_recode.description: Use raw_Race and raw_Ethnicity, applying the source release coding scheme to reconstruct mutually exclusive black, white, hispanic, asian/pacific islander, other, and unknown categories before analysis.

search_outcome.label: Search outcome definition
search_outcome.rationale: Which recorded action should count as a search for the search rate?  [found by: direct]

search_conducted.label: Any recorded search
search_conducted.description: Define the binary outcome as search_conducted = 1 versus search_conducted = 0; exclude rows with missing search_conducted.

person_search.label: Person search
person_search.description: Define the binary outcome as search_person = 1 versus search_person = 0; exclude rows with missing search_person.

vehicle_search.label: Vehicle search
vehicle_search.description: Define the binary outcome as search_vehicle = 1 versus search_vehicle = 0; exclude rows with missing search_vehicle.

search_or_frisk.label: Search or frisk
search_or_frisk.description: Define the binary outcome as 1 when search_conducted = 1 or frisk_performed = 1, and 0 otherwise; exclude rows missing both component indicators.

race_adjustment_model.label: Adjustment and rate-comparison model
race_adjustment_model.rationale: Should race-group search rates be compared without adjustment or conditional on recorded stop characteristics?  [found by: direct]

crude_rate_comparison.label: Unadjusted group-rate comparison
crude_rate_comparison.description: For each race category, report searches divided by stops and compare the categories using a single omnibus comparison of the unadjusted rates; do not include covariates.

unadjusted_logistic.label: Unadjusted logistic regression
unadjusted_logistic.description: Fit a binary logistic regression of the selected search outcome on race category alone, reporting race-group predicted probabilities or odds ratios.

adjusted_logistic.label: Adjusted logistic regression
adjusted_logistic.description: Fit a binary logistic regression of the selected search outcome on race category, subject_age, subject_sex, reason_for_stop, county_name, department_name, and calendar date; report race-group adjusted predicted probabilities.

contrast_structure.label: Race contrasts
contrast_structure.rationale: What race comparison should constitute the primary test?  [found by: direct]

global_omnibus.label: Global omnibus comparison
global_omnibus.description: Test the null that all included race categories have the same search probability, using one joint race comparison; do not make a specific race the reference for the primary claim.

white_reference.label: Each category versus white
white_reference.description: Use white as the reference category and report separate contrasts of black, hispanic, asian/pacific islander, and other versus white; omit unknown unless it is included by the race-definition decision.

all_pairwise.label: All pairwise race comparisons
all_pairwise.description: Report a separate comparison for every pair of included race categories, rather than one global comparison or only comparisons with white.

dependence_handling.label: Dependence and uncertainty calculation
dependence_handling.rationale: How should repeated stops associated with the same officer or department affect uncertainty estimates?  [found by: direct]

iid.label: Independent-stop standard errors
iid.description: Treat rows as independent when computing standard errors, confidence intervals, and test statistics.

cluster_officer.label: Cluster by officer
cluster_officer.description: Compute heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors clustered by officer_id_hash, allowing arbitrary dependence among stops handled by the same officer.

cluster_department.label: Cluster by department
cluster_department.description: Compute heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors clustered by department_name, allowing dependence within reporting departments.

two_way_cluster.label: Two-way officer and department clustering
two_way_cluster.description: Compute two-way cluster-robust standard errors using officer_id_hash and department_name as the two clustering dimensions.
